description: A short tusk ground flat on one side. Gnashjaw does that on purpose, to boulders, for hours.
lore: The flat is the point. All that grinding leaves one face of the tusk as smooth as slate and about as willing to take a mark, and a scribe with a fine point and a steady hand can put a hundred words on one and know they will still be legible in three hundred years. Nothing else the trade handles will hold ink that long.

[[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] buys them and does not use them. Four sit blank on the shelf over her desk, bought at twenty-six gold apiece out of a purse that does not run to it. Asked why, she says she is saving them for names. Pressed at [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]]'s fire on which names, she said the ones that are not going to be said out loud, and turned the talk to the weather, and has not been pressed again.
gm_notes: Four blank tusks are a standing hook. One of the names Bettany is holding a blank for is Sigrun's withheld word; she has never written it and will not without being given it.
